scenes.name: coffee-shop-street-workers
scenes.prompt: Bespoke editorial photograph. WIDE ESTABLISHING SHOT from the street outside a small third-wave coffee shop at first light — the storefront is on the left third of the frame, workers actively placing a young Japanese Zelkova sapling (approximately 1.2m tall, burlap root ball visible, wood tree stakes and coir tie-wire beside the hole) into a fresh sidewalk cutout in the center-right of the frame. Workers wear canvas-tan work jackets and burnt-sienna beanies (urban forestry crew). Through the shop window on the left, the young woman with dark hair in a low knot is barely visible in warm interior light, silhouetted at her table. Street details: nordic-oak floors visible through window, La Marzocco Linea Classic AV espresso machine as a warm silhouette, one antique brass Edison-bulb pendant glowing. Cobblestone sidewalk in the foreground, morning mist in the middle distance, other quiet independent storefronts receding into background. HIGH-FASHION EDITORIAL LIGHTING: Peter Lindbergh cool-morning street register. Sculptural east-facing morning key from off-frame right. Deep controlled fill on the shop facade shadow side. Kodak Vision3 500T warm film grain. Shot on ARRI ALEXA 65 with Zeiss Master Anamorphic 40mm. No text, no logos, no branded storefront signage. Bespoke. Contemplative. The technology this scene celebrates is invisible in the frame; only the life visible.

scenes.name: nyc-park-view-through-window
scenes.prompt: Bespoke editorial photograph. WIDE VIEW LOOKING THROUGH the floor-to-ceiling multi-pane arched pre-war window on Central Park South at mid-morning in October. The window mullion is a thin blackened-steel grid visible in the top and bottom edges of the frame. Central Park spreads wide below in the middle-distance, October autumn canopy in yellow-orange and burnt-sienna. ONE specific mature London Plane tree (Platanus × acerifolia) dominates the middle-left of the view with its distinctive mottled camouflage bark clearly visible on trunk far below. Upper West Side pre-war skyline stretches across the far background at gentle atmospheric haze — limestone facades, water towers, one distant church spire. No people in the frame at all — the office is empty, the view is the subject. Sunlight rakes across the park canopy from camera-right, catching the tops of the trees. HIGH-FASHION EDITORIAL LIGHTING: Bradford Young Selma register — patient light, deep autumn palette. Warm-cool contrast between interior shadow (foreground window mullion) and sunlit park (middle-distance). Kodak Vision3 500T warm film grain. Shot on ARRI ALEXA 65 with Zeiss Master Anamorphic 40mm at f/2.8. No text, no logos, no readable signage. Bespoke. The city that the substrate quietly holds in place while its executives take their mid-morning.

scenes.name: amalfi-mediterranean-vista
scenes.prompt: Bespoke editorial photograph. VERY WIDE COASTAL VISTA at golden hour on the Amalfi Costiera between Positano and Praiano — the Mediterranean spreads infinite into hazy blue below, horizon line at approximately 40% from top of frame. Terraced hillsides descend to the sea in a series of dry-stone walls (mortar-free warm limestone field stones), lemon groves visible in middle-distance clinging to the terraces, olive groves further out. Small distant village of pale-ochre and terracotta houses clings to a headland in the far background right, a Roman-era church campanile visible. Two seagulls in the middle-distance sky. Golden hour sun cresting a cliff camera-right creates a long low warm raking light across the whole vista. NO PEOPLE, NO CARS in this frame — pure landscape, the coast itself. In the immediate foreground-right, one ancient Rotondella olive tree (approximately 500 years old, 3-5 gnarled trunks, silver-green foliage) barely visible in the corner, its crown reaching into the top-right of frame. HIGH-FASHION EDITORIAL LIGHTING: Bruce Weber coastal fashion crossed with Paolo Sorrentino contemplative-warm register. Sculptural golden-hour side-light. Warm rim on the olive canopy and the distant church. Deep controlled shadow on the terraces facing away from sun. Kodak Vision3 500T warm film grain. Shot on ARRI ALEXA 65 with Zeiss Master Anamorphic 40mm at f/4. No text, no branded signage. Bespoke. Majestic. Nostalgic. The endurance the substrate makes possible.
